## Solution

**Setup.** The standard embedding $RP^2 \hookrightarrow RP^5$ is the inclusion of the 2-skeleton in the standard CW structure (one cell in each dimension $0,1,\dots,5$). Since $RP^2$ is a subcomplex, the quotient $RP^5/RP^2$ is a CW complex and
$$H_q(RP^5, RP^2) \cong \widetilde{H}_q(RP^5/RP^2) \quad \text{for all } q.$$

**Homology of $RP^n$ with $\mathbb{Z}$ coefficients.** The cellular chain complex of $RP^n$ has $C_k = \mathbb{Z}$ for $0 \le k \le n$ with boundary $d_k = 1+(-1)^k$ (so $d_k = 0$ for $k$ odd, $d_k = 2$ for $k$ even). This gives:

| $q$ | $H_q(RP^2)$ | $H_q(RP^5)$ |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| 0   | $\mathbb{Z}$ | $\mathbb{Z}$ |
| 1   | $\mathbb{Z}/2$ | $\mathbb{Z}/2$ |
| 2   | $0$ | $0$ |
| 3   | $0$ | $\mathbb{Z}/2$ |
| 4   | $0$ | $0$ |
| 5   | $0$ | $\mathbb{Z}$ |

**Induced maps.** The inclusion $i: RP^2 \hookrightarrow RP^5$ is the inclusion of the 2-skeleton, so $i_*: H_q(RP^2) \to H_q(RP^5)$ is an isomorphism for $q = 0, 1$ (the chain complexes agree in those dimensions), and the zero map for $q = 2$ (both groups vanish).

**Long exact sequence of the pair $(RP^5, RP^2)$.** We compute $H_q(RP^5, RP^2) \cong \widetilde{H}_q(RP^5/RP^2)$ dimension by dimension.

*$q=0$:* $H_0(RP^2) \xrightarrow{\cong} H_0(RP^5) \to H_0(RP^5,RP^2) \to 0$. Since $i_*$ is an isomorphism, $H_0(RP^5,RP^2)=0$, so $H_0(RP^5/RP^2)=\mathbb{Z}$.

*$q=1$:* $H_1(RP^2)\xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(RP^5) \xrightarrow{j_*} H_1(RP^5,RP^2)\xrightarrow{\partial} H_0(RP^2)\xrightarrow{\cong} H_0(RP^5)$. Since $i_*$ on $H_1$ is surjective, $j_*=0$; since $i_*$ on $H_0$ is injective, $\partial=0$. Thus $H_1(RP^5,RP^2)=0$.

*$q=2$:* $0 \to 0 \to H_2(RP^5,RP^2) \xrightarrow{\partial} H_1(RP^2)\xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(RP^5)$. Since $i_*$ on $H_1$ is injective, $\partial=0$; since $j_*$ has domain $0$, $\ker\partial = \text{im}(j_*)=0$. Thus $H_2(RP^5,RP^2)=0$.

*$q=3$:* $0 \to \mathbb{Z}/2 \xrightarrow{j_*} H_3(RP^5,RP^2) \xrightarrow{\partial} 0$. Here $j_*$ is injective (kernel = image of $0$) and surjective ($\ker\partial = H_3(RP^5,RP^2)$ since $\partial$ maps to $0$). Thus $H_3(RP^5,RP^2)\cong\mathbb{Z}/2$.

*$q=4$:* $0\to 0\to H_4(RP^5,RP^2)\xrightarrow{\partial} 0$. So $H_4(RP^5,RP^2)=0$.

*$q=5$:* $0\to\mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{j_*} H_5(RP^5,RP^2)\xrightarrow{\partial} 0$. Here $j_*$ is injective and surjective, so $H_5(RP^5,RP^2)\cong\mathbb{Z}$.

*$q\ge 6$:* $H_q(RP^5,RP^2)=0$ since $RP^5$ has no cells in dimensions $\ge 6$.

**Verification via cellular chain complex of the quotient.** The quotient $RP^5/RP^2$ has cells in dimensions $0, 3, 4, 5$ (the cells of $RP^5$ not in $RP^2$, plus one $0$-cell from the collapsed $RP^2$). The cellular chain complex is:
$$0 \to \mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{\bar d_5} \mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{\bar d_4} \mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{\bar d_3} \mathbb{Z}\to 0 \qquad (\text{dimensions }5,4,3,0)$$
with $\bar d_5 = 0$ (degree $1+(-1)^5=0$), $\bar d_4 = 2$ (degree $1+(-1)^4=2$), $\bar d_3 = 0$ (target $C_2=0$). Computing:
- $H_5 = \ker(0)/0 = \mathbb{Z}$ ✓
- $H_4 = \ker(2)/\text{im}(0) = 0$ ✓
- $H_3 = \ker(0)/\text{im}(2) = \mathbb{Z}/2$ ✓
- $H_2 = H_1 = 0$ ✓
- $H_0 = \mathbb{Z}/0 = \mathbb{Z}$ ✓

Both methods agree.

## Result

$$H_q(RP^5/RP^2) = \begin{cases} \mathbb{Z} & q = 0,\\ 0 & q = 1,\\ 0 & q = 2,\\ \mathbb{Z}/2 & q = 3,\\ 0 & q = 4,\\ \mathbb{Z} & q = 5,\\ 0 & q \ge 6. \end{cases}$$
